# Apply filters to SQL queries

## Project description

In this scenario I aim to obtain specific information about employees, log in attempts made after business hours, which machines they are using and what departments they belong to.

## Retrieve after hours failed login attempts 
<img width="950" height="553" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f70a137c-3b4c-4ac0-842c-e7278c83af22" />

  I needed to view failed login attempts that were made after business hours. By selecting all from the log in attempts table I could view everything within it. I then filtered the resources by the time business hours ended and the failed log in attempts made. By using login\_time \> ’18:00’ I was able to view all log in attempts after 18:00 and by using success \= FALSE I was able to further my filter by only showing the failed attempts.

##


## Retrieve login attempts on specific dates

## <img width="845" height="418" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3126cff7-4a90-4535-a7f4-ddad2952802b" />
 Next, I investigated a suspicious event that occurred on 2022-05-09 I needed to retrieve all login attempts that occurred on that day as well as the day before, 2022-05-08. I did this by filtering the dates as such. WHERE login\_date \= ‘2022-05-09’ OR login\_date \= ‘2022-05-08’; This showed me all connections successfully and unsuccessfully made on both dates mentioned.  

## Retrieve login attempts outside of Mexico
<img width="809" height="402" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5f424e61-ac62-468d-a646-c084dfbe0821" />

Now I began investigating events that did not originate in Mexico. In my previous query all failed connection attempts were made from the US, USA and CANADA. I used WHERE NOT country LIKE ‘MEX%’; To remove any text with MEX from the country column to further investigate the connections being attempted.

## Retrieve employees in Marketing 
<img width="827" height="364" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ad9c52b9-85b4-47af-bc07-975b142d26b1" />

Since I was able to see usernames of connection attempts made, I was able to narrow down my search to a department basis. Filtering by departments allowed me to see which office each employee was in. I did this by doing WHERE department \= ‘Marketing’ AND office LIKE ‘EAST%’;  Adding a % wildcard to EAST allowed me to view each office within the east area. 

## Retrieving employees in Finance or Sales
<img width="841" height="511" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aff58ce2-02da-44e6-a8f0-dc34f7744fef" />

The team now needs to perform an update to the computers of all employees in the finance and sales department. In order to find all employees in each department I used   
WHERE department \= ‘Finance’ OR department \= ‘Sales’; This filter showed me each employee within the sales and finance department.

## 

## Retrieve all employees not in IT
<img width="823" height="423" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/603875cc-68fe-424e-90c1-db4bdf1f5f77" />
 
One final update needed to be made. We had already pushed that update for IT and need to inform all employees who are not in that department of the upcoming update and possible downtime. To show all employees not in the Information Technology department I filtered the employees table by using the query WHERE NOT department \= ‘Information Technology’; 

## Summary

In this lab I used AND, OR and NOT filters to narrow searches and tables down to the pertinent info I needed at the time.
